attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post. He agrees with Musk's point but asserts the change himself.

semantics.note: Faithful past-tense observation. The 'since Musk's contributions' baseline is kept as a qualifier.

contract.note: The plain reading ties 'mission' to the commitments the post names: nonprofit status, openness, and freedom from financial return. Separating operating commitments from the ultimate purpose is fair and ordinary. The result depends on which component counts.

evidence.note: 2015 founding announcement. Sets the baseline: nonprofit, free of financial-return obligations.
2019 capped-profit LP with investor and employee returns materially revises the 'unconstrained by financial return' and nonprofit-only commitments. Company disclosure.
Charter (2018) keeps a humanity-wide beneficiary and a primary duty to humanity. This shows continuity in the public-benefit purpose. Company disclosure.
Interested retrospective account from 2024-03-05. It places the for-profit discussions during Musk's tenure. It does not disprove a change from the founding commitments.

reviews.rationale: Part holds: by 2019 OpenAI replaced its nonprofit-only, no-financial-return operating model with a capped-profit entity (e2). Part fails: the stated public-benefit purpose and fiduciary duty to humanity continued (e3, e2), which counts against change in that component under the contract. The evidence consists of company disclosures.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: 'That mission' refers to the original mission from the early days. The normalisation is faithful.

contract.note: Reading 'strayed' as a material, documented departure from the founding commitments is fair. The contract also accounts for the 'when applicable' qualifier on openness. The speaker gave no threshold, so the result turns on which component of the mission counts.

evidence.note: Founding announcement baseline: nonprofit, free of financial return, encourages publication.
2015 certificate. Its openness commitment is qualified ('when applicable'), and it sets a public-benefit purpose.

2020 API announcement gives commercialization as a reason to withhold models instead of open-sourcing them. This is a departure from the original operating approach, though accessibility and misuse reasons are also cited.
2023 testimony describes continued nonprofit control, profit caps, and a public-benefit fiduciary duty. This counts against departure in governance and purpose. Company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: Part holds: commercialization and API-only release, motivated partly by revenue (e3), depart from the founding operating model (e1). Part fails: nonprofit control, capped profits, and a public-benefit duty remained in 2023 (e4), and openness was qualified from the start (e2). The packet cannot settle whether restricted release breached the 'when applicable' qualifier.
